Bally Bagayoko, mayor of Saint-Denis, speaks to journalists after being evacuated amid clashes between protesters and French police during a demonstration, part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades, in Paris, France on Oct 6, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Abdul Saboor)

Bally Bagayoko, mayor of Saint-Denis, is evacuated amid clashes between protesters and French police during a demonstration, part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades, in Paris, France on Oct 6, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Abdul Saboor)

The wave of student protests , which began in Paris' marginalised suburbs, has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace French President Emmanuel Macron. There have been more than 6,000 arrests and dozens of student injuries since the protests began. Rights groups and unions accuse the police of using heavy-handed tactics against minors, including the use of batons, tear gas and non-lethal flashball guns. Authorities say hundreds of police officers have also been injured, schools have been burned or ransacked, and teachers and members of the public have been attacked. The town of Saint-Denis, where poverty levels are more than double the national average, was one of the first sites of student protests in late September over overcrowded and unsanitary classrooms, teacher shortages and unequal opportunities. "Protests are not new here, they happen at every start of the academic year," Bagayoko said. "The Republican promise (of equality) - in particular for the working-class neighbourhoods, and also rural areas - is not respected." He said the government should prioritise investing in education and levy heavier taxes on billionaires. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Wednesday that the government would review demands made by students and present proposals at the end of October, but gave no details. The government has suggested that LFI politicians were behind the protests, an accusation that Bagayoko dismissed as insulting to the young protesters. A father of four, he said that "the high school children who were in the street could be my children ... it is my responsibility to be at their side".

item.title: ＴｉｋＴｏｋ、未成年に機能しない安全策の実験 ＮＹ州が訴訟で主張
item.description:
Diana Novak Jones
[７日 ロイター] - 米ニューヨーク州が動画投稿アプリ「ＴｉｋＴｏｋ（ティックト...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＴｉｋＴｏｋ、未成年に機能しない安全策の実験　ＮＹ州が訴訟で主張 10:41 配信

２月２０日、ドイツのボンで撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Jana Rodenbusch）

Diana Novak Jones

[７日 ロイター] - 米ニューヨーク州が動画投稿アプリ「ＴｉｋＴｏｋ（ティックトック）」を相手取った訴訟で、７日に公開された訴状の一部によると、同社は安全機能を有効にしようとした数千人の利用者に、実際には作動しない機能を提供する実験を行っていた。

それによると、「ゴースト」またはプラセボ（偽薬）と呼ばれる実験で、望まないコンテンツや有害な恐れのあるコンテンツを避けるため、おすすめ表示をリセットする「アルゴ・リフレッシュ」などの安全機能を使おうとした利用者の中から、１０代の若者や子どもを含む数千人が選ばれた。対象者は機能を有効にしたと思っていたが、正常に作動する機能を提供された利用者とは異なり、表示されるコンテンツは変わらなかった。

今回公開された主張は、ニューヨーク州のレティシア・ジェームズ司法長官が起こした訴訟の一部。ＴｉｋＴｏｋを巡っては子どもを依存させるようサービスを設計し、安全性について利用者に誤解を与えているとして、同州など全米各地の州で２０を超える訴訟が提起されている。同社が運営の詳細を公にしないよう求めてきたため、各地の州の訴訟では多くの文書が非公開となるか、大幅に黒塗りされている。

訴状は、ＴｉｋＴｏｋが安全性を最優先事項とし、子どもや１０代の若者に適したサービスだと利用者に説明する一方で、望まないコンテンツなどを避けたいと明確に意思表示した利用者を含め、一部の利用者が特定の安全機能を使えないよう意図的にしていたと主張している。

ＴｉｋＴｏｋの広報担当者は声明で「われわれはサービスを継続的に改善している。そのため、大半の企業と同様、利用体験を検証し、実際の環境でどのように機能するかを把握するため、新製品や新機能を定期的にテストしている」と説明した。

item.title: 10月ロイター企業調査：26年度最終損益、上期は3割超が期初予想から上振れ 下期見通しは慎重
item.description:
Tetsushi Kajimoto
［東京 ８日 ロイター］ - １０月のロイター企業調査で、２０２６年度の最終損益が...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
10月ロイター企業調査：26年度最終損益、上期は3割超が期初予想から上振れ　下期見通しは慎重 10:33 配信

2024年11月、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Tetsushi Kajimoto

［東京　８日　ロイター］ - １０月のロイター企業調査で、２０２６年度の最終損益が期初見込みに比べてどのように推移しているか聞いたところ、上期は３割超が「改善する」と回答し、「悪化する」とした約２割を上回った。下期に関しては、改善予想は２割にとどまり、悪化予想を若干下回り、慎重な見通しが示された。収益に対するリスクは、４割近くが米イラン戦争による原油市場の動向を挙げ、金利や為替の変動、米貿易政策を上回り最も多かった。

調査は９月１８日━１０月２日に実施。発送企業５０８社（資本金１０億円以上の上場・非上場企業、除く金融業）のうち２１５社が回答した。

上期純損益が期初見込みと比べ「改善する」との答えは全体の３２％となり、「悪化する」の２２％を上回った。残る４６％が、「おおよそ予想通り」とした。下期については、期初見込みより「改善を予想」との回答が２０％と、上期よりも低い割合にとどまり、「悪化を予想」と答えた２２％もやや下回った。「おおよそ期初見込み通り」との回答は５８％に上った。

収益見通しに対するリスクは、「米・イラン戦争による原油市場の不安定化」との回答が最も多く、３７％を占めた。為替変動が２１％、金利上昇が１９％で続いた。米国の関税など貿易政策による影響との回答は７％にとどまった。

企業からは「原油・エネルギーコストの不安定化に伴う原材料費・物流費の上昇が最大の懸念。加えて、米国の通商政策、中国市場の需要減速、労務費上昇分の価格転嫁の進歩が下期業績を左右する」（ゴムメーカー）との指摘があった。「中東問題が続けば備蓄原油の枯渇を含め、国内製造業に大きな影響を及ぼす可能性がある」（情報サービス業）との懸念も示された。

原油高に伴うエネルギーコストの上昇に加え「金利上昇局面における投資抑制による国内セメント需要減少がリスク要因」（窯業）との声も聞かれた。

「為替も金利も戦争も米国の貿易政策も、すべてがリスク要因となっており、正直何を最も警戒すべきなのか、選択すること自体が難しい状況。それ以上に問題なのは、何かが起きた時の市場の反応があまりにも急激で振れ幅も大きすぎること」（輸送用機器）と訴える企業もあった。

「自然災害増加に伴う自社設備維持費の増加」（放送）がリスク要因との指摘も出た。

item.title: 10月ロイター企業調査：退職金制度14％が見直し、8％が検討中 背景に定年延長や人材獲得強化
item.description:
Yusuke Ogawa
［東京 ８日 ロイター］ - １０月のロイター企業調査で退職金制度の運用状況を聞いたところ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
10月ロイター企業調査：退職金制度14％が見直し、8％が検討中　背景に定年延長や人材獲得強化 10:28 配信

都内で５月撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Yusuke Ogawa

［東京　８日　ロイター］ - １０月のロイター企業調査で退職金制度の運用状況を聞いたところ、２０２０年度以降に制度を見直した企業と、見直しを検討している企業を合わせると４６社となり、回答企業の２割を超えた。定年延長などへの対応に加え、優秀な人材の確保を目的に制度を変更する動きも出ている。

調査は９月１８日から１０月２日に実施。５０８社に発送し、２１５社から回答を得た。

制度を「見直した」と答えた企業は３０社で回答企業の約１４％。「見直していないが検討中」は１６社で８％だった。

制度を見直した企業に変更内容を複数回答で聞いたところ、「企業年金制度の新設」と「退職給付額を増額」がそれぞれ６社だった。一方で、「退職給付額を減額」は４社、確定給付型（ＤＢ）から確定拠出型（ＤＣ）への移行などを含む「その他」が１６社だった。

制度を見直した、または検討している理由を複数回答で聞くと、「定年延長・高齢者雇用への対応」が１９社で最も多く、「優秀な人材の確保」が１８社、「賃金体系の見直し」が１６社で続いた。

非製造業に限ると、「優秀な人材の確保」が最多だった。人材の採用や定着が課題となる中、退職金を含む待遇を見直す必要性が高まっていることがうかがえる。

退職給付額を減額した４社は、いずれも代わりに社員の給与を増やした。このうち３社は全社員、１社は２０─３０代社員の給与を引き上げた。物価高で生活コストが上昇する中、退職金を前払いするなどして月例給与を厚くする企業も出ている。

また、転職機会の増加を背景に、自由回答では「退職金に重きを置く制度は時代に合わない」（卸売）、「長く勤めた人への報酬から、多様なキャリアを前提とした資産形成の選択肢として設計すべきだ」（ゴム）などの声が聞かれた。

（小川祐介　グラフィックス作成：照井裕子　編集：久保信博）

item.title: 経常黒字、8月は12％増の4兆620億円 海外直接投資益の黒字拡大
item.description:
Tetsushi Kajimoto
［東京 ８日 ロイター］ - 財務省が８日発表した８月の国際収支状況速報によると、...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
経常黒字、8月は12％増の4兆620億円　海外直接投資益の黒字拡大 10:09 配信

東京湾で8月撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Tetsushi Kajimoto

［東京　８日　ロイター］ - 財務省が８日発表した８月の国際収支状況速報によると、経常収支は４兆０６２０億円の黒字だった。黒字額は前年同月から１２％増え、ロイターが集計した民間調査機関の予測中央値３兆１９４６億円を大きく上回った。

内訳をみると、貿易収支は６８７７億円の赤字と、前年の黒字から赤字に転化した。原粗油等の輸入増が背景にある。

サービス収支は１１５８億円の赤字で、赤字幅は前年から１５０９億円縮小した。訪日外国人客数は減少したものの、堅調な訪日需要で旅行収支の黒字幅が拡大した。

第１次所得収支は５兆１３３２億円の黒字と、黒字額は前年比で２１．６％増え、比較可能な１９８５年以降で過去最大を記録した。海外子会社からの配当金受け取りなど直接投資収益の黒字幅拡大が主因。為替でドル／円が前年比７．５％上昇、ユーロ／円が７．２％上昇と、円安が進行したことも第１次所得収支の大幅な黒字を支えた。

農中総合研究所の南武志・理事研究員は、円安は一服したものの、引き続き海外からの所得収支の黒字増加が原油高による貿易赤字を相殺していると分析。所得収支の黒字が国内に還流されずに海外の再投資に振り向けられる傾向にあることは「人口減少下の国内需給を見ると、ある意味仕方がない」とした。

＊財務省の発表資料は以下のＵＲＬでご覧になれます。

http://www.mof.go.jp/international_policy/reference/balance_of_payments/release_date.htm

item.title: Shares slip as bond bashing rumbles on
item.description: Global shares slid on Thursday as strains in sovereign bond markets were aggravated by a jump in oil prices and reports that some major tech firms were seeking to raise billions in debt in direct competition for limited funding.
item.dc:creator: Lawrence Delevingne, Marc Jones, Wayne Cole
item.content:encoded: Global shares slid on Thursday as strains in sovereign bond markets were aggravated by a jump in oil prices and reports that some major [USN:FWN45T25Y TEXT:"tech firms"] were seeking to raise billions in debt in direct competition for limited funding. Wall Street got off to a [USN:L4N45U12K TEXT:"bumpy start"], with the S&P 500 (.SPX) down about 0.3% and the Nasdaq (.IXIC) off nearly 0.5%, as the US 10-year rate nudged higher again and as Europe's traders sent their region's stocks to a near 3-month low (.STOXX) amid extensive handwringing over France and other heavily indebted countries' finances. A whole flock of European Central Bank policymakers also issued fresh inflation warnings to feed the [USN:L6N45T0G5 TEXT:"debate"] on its next move, while oil prices reared up more than 4% too following an increase in [USN:L1N45U01Q TEXT:"attacks on shipping"] in the Gulf. While lofty US Treasury yields underpinned the dollar, the euro struggled near a 17-month low as the concerns over "[USN:L1N45T0KZ TEXT:"le spread" in France"] continued to affect Italian and Greek debt, as well as parts of the banking sector. CLIMB IN BORROWING COSTS "Markets are going to be watchful if that contagion continues," said Kiran Ganesh, a multi-asset strategist at UBS Global Wealth Management. "At this stage, the markets would be most comforted by monetary intervention," he added, referring to the ECB buying bonds to ease the market strains. The steady climb in borrowing costs left the benchmark US Treasury yield just off its recent 24-year peak and put equities on the defensive. The pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) fell as much as 1% to its lowest since June before clawing back roughly half of the ground, while the CAC-40's drop in Paris (.FCHI) left it 12% down from an August record high. European banks suffered as well, with the finance index down (.SX7P) nearly 1.5% by mid-afternoon as Deutsche Bank (DBKGn.DE) , Santander (SAN.MC) , Societe Generale (SOGN.PA) and Unicredit (CRDI.MI) all fell for a second day. Overnight in Asia, Japan's Nikkei (.N225) had shed 1.4% and South Korea's chipmaker-heavy KOSPI (.KS11) slumped 2.6%. AI DEBT RUSH In commodity markets, Brent futures [USN:L1N45U031 TEXT:"rose back"] to $104.5 a barrel in their biggest jump in a month, while US crude futures added 4.3% to $92.1 a barrel. The US quarterly earnings season picks up pace next week with big banks including JPMorgan (JPM.N) set to report results. Optimism around strong earnings has buoyed US stocks lately despite shaky geopolitical developments and concerns about rising interest rates. The tech and energy sectors are expected to report the biggest quarterly earnings growth, while the broader S&P 500 (.SPX) is expected to post a punchy 30.6% increase in quarterly earnings, according to LSEG data. Debt remains a strong underwater current though. The Wall Street Journal had added to media reports on Wednesday that SpaceX (SPCX.O) , Broadcom (AVGO.O) and Oracle (ORCL.N) were all looking to raise serious money to buy high-end AI chips. Broadcom was looking for $50 billion in financing, while [USN:L6N45S1CR TEXT:"SpaceX"] was planning to issue $30 billion in investment-grade debt and raise $10 billion in loans to buy chips from Nvidia (NVDA.O) , which is a major shareholder in SpaceX. The news saw credit default insurance on SpaceX jump to record highs, while its shares and bonds lost ground. "Part of the reason why (equity) markets are OK right now is the 30% earnings growth expectations," Boston Partners strategist Mike Mullaney said. But with the so-called AI-focused "hyperscalers" expected to spend more than $10 trillion in terms of capital expenditure — or 8% of US GDP — "the math (on earnings and company valuations) doesn't work for me". SOVEREIGN BONDS VS CORPORATE DEBT Still, the fact much of this money will be spent on AI equipment is set to be positive for earnings in the semiconductor and memory sectors. [USN:L1N45T115 TEXT:"Samsung Electronics"] (005930.KS) on Thursday projected a 783% jump in third-quarter operating profit to 107.4 trillion won ($80.17 billion), though its shares lost 2.4%. TSMC (2330.TW) , the world's largest contract chipmaker, also reported a [USN:L6N45U0AF TEXT:"record third-quarter revenue"] of T$1.49 trillion ($46.71 billion), up 50% from the year-earlier period. Its shares fell 1.35%. All this corporate debt is coming at a time when sovereign bond markets are being sorely tested by inflation fears, ever-widening budget deficits and rising cash rates. Minutes of the [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"Federal Reserve's"] last meeting released on Wednesday showed "most" members considered another rate hike likely by year-end, though they would approach each meeting with an open mind. Markets imply just a 21% chance the Fed will move again this month, but are nearly 80% priced for a rise in December. "We expect a second Fed hike in December, though we see a strong chance the Fed ultimately concludes further tightening is unnecessary," analysts at Goldman Sachs wrote in a note. The prospect of a pause in tightening helped keep 2-year Treasury yields at 4.80% , while 10-year yields crept up to 5.28% , having hit a 24-year top of 5.36% overnight. Strains in the French bond market led [USN:L8N45T074 TEXT:"Bank of France head Emmanuel Moulin"] to acknowledge the country's economic situation was serious on Wednesday, but he said it did not need help from the European Central Bank. Investors reacted by offloading the euro, which was pinned at $1.119 after having lost 0.6% on Wednesday. A break of the recent low at $1.1161 would risk a retreat to $1.1065. The dollar was the main beneficiary of the single currency's woes and its index rose to 102.32 , near an 18-month peak. It was steady on the yen at 158.18 , with the Japanese currency protected by the threat of intervention. Non-interest-bearing gold has suffered as yields climbed, but managed a modest 0.3% [USN:L1N45U0DB TEXT:"bounce"] to $4,122 an ounce having found bids at two-month lows.

item.title: Türkiye sending technical, defensive support to Saudi Arabia to help fight Houthis, officials say
item.description: A Turkish official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the support expected from Türkiye was only in the form of military equipment, intelligence sharing, and weapons systems.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Türkiye sending technical, defensive support to Saudi Arabia to help fight Houthis, officials say

A Turkish official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the support expected from Türkiye was only in the form of military equipment, intelligence sharing, and weapons systems.

Members of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces fire a tank during what they say are clashes with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis in a location given as near Al-Hazm, Yemen, Sep 9, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Media Centre Of The Yemeni Armed Forces)

FAST

ANKARA: Türkiye is sending mainly defensive and technical support to Saudi Arabia to help it fight Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis , two officials said on Wednesday (Oct 7), after the NATO member and Pakistan pledged to act on the collective defence commitment of their newly formed alliance. Türkiye , Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in August , under which an armed attack on one member constituted an attack on all. They have been working to set the parameters of the new alliance and have held political and military meetings in response to the Houthi attacks. On Monday, the countries said they had agreed to move immediately to implement their collective defence commitments and ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia . Türkiye , which has NATO's second-largest army and a robust defence industry, has condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia , voiced willingness to help meet Riyadh's technical military needs, and agreed to join a Saudi -led coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.

CNA Games

A Turkish official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the support expected from Türkiye was only in the form of military equipment, intelligence sharing, and weapons systems, adding that no other form of deployment had taken place as part of the alliance so far.

DRONE OPERATORS, FINE-TUNING DEFENSIVE MEASURES Officials have said that Turkish support for Saudi Arabia - including air defence systems - would largely be in a bilateral capacity for now, as Türkiye's parliament has not officially ratified the joint pact. The amount and nature of the support would increase after ratification, they have said. A US official briefed on the matter said that Türkiye had so far decided to send capabilities that were broadly defensive , including strategic planning support and help with logistics. The official said the assistance included drone operators and help with fine-tuning defensive measures, as well as intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, speaking to state media after an extraordinary meeting of the Mecca alliance in Riyadh, said the sides had discussed what support to provide Saudi Arabia to help its defensive capabilities. "We had our Defence Minister and Chief of General Staff with us, and they especially provided very fruitful views on military issues, operational issues, and technical matters," he said on Monday.

Related:

Houthis say Saudi Arabia launches dozens of strikes on Yemen capital

Three in four families go hungry in parts of Yemen from new fighting

Omer Celik, spokesman for Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party, said later on Wednesday that the Mecca pact was expected to be submitted to parliament for ratification "in a few days", adding that the process on further steps would become clear then. Pakistani and regional officials have said Ankara and Islamabad have provided Saudi Arabia with military equipment that the kingdom is using in Yemen. This week, Yemeni government forces with Saudi -led coalition air support launched a counter-offensive to recapture strategic territory near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, an international shipping route for energy exports and other trade. Officials had told Reuters last week that Saudi Arabia was planning an offensive against the Houthis , with options being considered including a coastal push to secure the Red Sea shipping route or an assault on multiple fronts.

item.title: Christa Pike 'angry and confused' about Tennessee's failed execution effort, lawyers say
item.description: Her lawyers said she has pneumonia, severe swelling and difficulty eating and moving her arms, while Tennessee has suspended executions for the rest of the year.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Christa Pike 'angry and confused' about Tennessee's failed execution effort, lawyers say

Her lawyers said she has pneumonia, severe swelling and difficulty eating and moving her arms, while Tennessee has suspended executions for the rest of the year.

A picture taken on December 4, 2007 shows death row inmate Christa Pike entering a Knox County Criminal Court in Knoxville, Tennessee, US, obtained by Reuters on Sep 30, 2026. (File photo: J Miles Cary/ Knoxville News Sentinel/USA Today Network via Reuters)

08 Oct 2026 03:39AM (Updated: 08 Oct 2026 06:39AM)

FAST

WASHINGTON: Christa Pike , sentenced to death for a 1995 murder, awoke "angry and confused" in a hospital this week with a long recuperation ahead after surviving Tennessee's botched effort to execute her, her lawyers said on Wednesday (Oct 7). A week ago, Pike , 50, was taken from the execution chamber to a Nashville hospital, unconscious, critically ill and with severe arm injuries after two injections of the caustic barbiturate pentobarbital failed to kill her at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution. As late as Monday, her lawyers believed Pike was brain dead and that life support would be removed the next day following the second botched execution in Tennessee this year, which has renewed scrutiny of capital punishment in the US. "But on Tuesday, to the shock of everyone, including me, including her team, and including the medical team, Christa woke up and began talking," Randall Spivey, one of her lawyers, told reporters after a court hearing on Wednesday, where a judge ordered Tennessee officials to preserve syringes and other evidence from the botched execution.

"She is angry and confused about everything right now," Spivey said. "She is very aware that the state tried to execute her." Governor Bill Lee has suspended all executions for the rest of the year while investigators look into the botched executions of Pike and of Tony Carruthers in May, when prison officials were unable to set up intravenous lines. Pike remains very sick and shackled to her hospital bed, facing a long road to recovery, her lawyers said. She cannot swallow or eat, has pneumonia, cannot move her "tremendously swollen" hands or arms, and it is unclear if she will regain her lost mobility, they said. Although she still has "cognitive confusion," the lawyers said, she has been speaking with those around her. "She has wanted to know what's happened, and she's asked about several people," Spivey said. "She's asked about the victim's family." Pike was sentenced to death for her role as a teenager in the 1995 torture and murder of her 19-year-old schoolmate Colleen Slemmer. She is the first person known to have survived a "completed execution attempt" in the US, her lawyers say, calling it a violation of the Constitution's prohibition on cruel and unusual punishments.

A UNIQUE CASE Pike 's lawyers are unexpectedly continuing their litigation against state officials, seeking to pierce the secrecy that normally surrounds execution procedures in Tennessee and other states. Earlier on Wednesday, a judge in Davidson County Chancery Court, I'Ashea Myles, agreed to order Tennessee officials to preserve all evidence from the failed execution, including syringes, drug packaging and lot numbers, catheters, intravenous lines and gurney restraints. The all-female execution team requested by Pike used at least seven needles during a gruelling ordeal that lasted more than two hours, and one needle was bent 90 degrees when it was pulled out, her lawyers said. Myles largely sided with Pike 's lawyers at the end of Wednesday's hearing, describing the litigation, which began in January in an effort to prevent the scheduled execution, as unusual because no one had anticipated Pike surviving. "This case is unique, to say the least," Myles said. She also ordered the state to preserve internal communications about the attempted execution, including incident reports, witness accounts and encrypted messages. She has yet to rule on a request by Pike 's lawyers that the Tennessee Department of Correction let them take any residual traces of the execution drugs for chemical analysis. The Tennessee Department of Correction has opposed what it says is a "duplicative and unnecessary" preservation order, arguing it is already legally required to preserve all evidence and that it was already willing to share most, if not all, of what Pike 's lawyers sought.

Related:

Tennessee prison chief resigns after failed execution

Christa Pike gets 'life-saving medical care' after surviving Tennessee execution

Tennessee and other US states have long struggled to acquire execution drugs. They cannot be obtained from major pharmaceutical companies because of a European trade ban on companies that sell products for use in torture or executions. Tennessee, like other states, has turned to small, largely unregulated compounding pharmacies to make small batches of the drugs, promising to hide their identity. "Today's hearing was about transparency, about why Christa , the courts, the media and the public should not simply take the state's word about what happened last Wednesday," Luke Ihnen, another lawyer for Pike , told reporters after the judge's ruling. He repeated the demand that Tennessee Governor Bill Lee commute Pike 's sentence to life in prison and never attempt to execute her again. A spokesperson for Lee, who denied a clemency appeal two days before the failed execution, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Pike 's lawyers had sought an alternative to lethal injections, saying her small veins and related medical conditions made her afraid that something would go wrong.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Britain's BBC, Channel 4 discuss broader tie-up to cut costs, sources say
item.description: Britain's BBC and Channel 4 have held preliminary talks with the government about a broader tie-up of some operations, two people with direct knowledge of the discussions said, in a potential shake-up of the country's public broadcasters.
item.dc:creator: Amy-Jo Crowley
item.content:encoded: Britain's BBC and Channel 4 have held preliminary talks with the government about a broader tie-up of some operations, two people with direct knowledge of the discussions said, in a potential shake-up of the country's public broadcasters. One option under discussion would combine Channel 4's advertising operations, channels including E4 and Film4, and its video-on-demand services, with UKTV, a commercial subsidiary of the BBC, the people told Reuters. A merged entity could be equally owned by the BBC and Channel 4 and represent a broader tie-up than the one previously indicated by BBC Director General Matt Brittin to include Channel 4 content in the BBC's iPlayer, the people said. The talks could intensify next year depending on what progress the BBC makes towards [USN:L8N43G0OI TEXT:"a new funding deal"] with the government, one of the people said, adding that the assets included in the potential joint venture could be expanded. The joint venture under consideration would not include the Channel 4 flagship broadcast channel, which could benefit from fees from the joint venture, the people said. The move would be aimed at cutting costs and helping secure the future of the public broadcasters as linear viewing declines and larger streaming companies [USN:L6N43U0UJ TEXT:"account for more"] of global advertising spend, the people said. A BBC spokesperson declined to comment. "But as we've said before we believe increased collaboration between all (public service broadcasters) is vital to ensure the industry thrives in a highly competitive global market place," the BBC spokesperson said. A Channel 4 spokesperson said: "We won't be commenting on any speculation but we welcome and support greater collaboration between Public Service Media and strongly believe working together can strengthen impact, innovation and sustainability in UK broadcasting. Channel 4 and the BBC already have a successful commercial relationship, involving ad sales for UKTV and the carriage of U on 4Streaming." Claire Enders, founder and chief executive of Enders Analysis, said the idea of a tie-up between BBC Studios and Channel 4 was "a perennial that flowered every so often". Although BBC Studios could end up as the ultimate home for Channel 4, Priya Dogra, who became Channel 4 CEO in March, had already taken steps to improve its financial footing, such as winning Skydance-owned Channel 5's advertising sales business, Enders said. "We're very far from a situation where Channel 4 is a failing firm," Enders added. DISCUSSING A DEEPER TIE-UP Channel 4 is government-owned but funded by advertisements, while the publicly owned BBC is mainly funded by a licence paid by TV-watching households. The talks involve UK Government Investments (UKGI), the entity responsible for managing publicly owned assets such as Channel 4, the people said. The plans could help Channel 4 and the BBC save costs, bringing some operations under one management and gaining a bigger slice of a consolidating market, the people said. UKGI declined to comment. If it went ahead, such a move would represent one of the biggest shake-ups for the broadcasters since Britain [USN:S8N31X084 TEXT:"scrapped"] plans to sell Channel 4 in 2023. Former Prime Minister Boris Johnson's government had announced the sale in 2022, triggering a backlash from lawmakers and the broadcasting industry. The two broadcasters had already been discussing partnerships around content sharing, such as a [USN:L8N45L0ZF TEXT:"potential plan"] to carry Channel 4 content on iPlayer. Channel 4 already carries UKTV content such as "The Office" and "Red Dwarf" on its streaming platform and manages ad sales for UKTV under a long-standing agreement. While it has ruled out merging with the BBC, it is open to sharing content on the iPlayer streaming service, Channel 4's CEO Priya Dogra [USN:L8N45L0ZF TEXT:"said at an industry event last month"]. Channel 4 and the BBC are pursuing cost-cutting, including through job reductions. The BBC [USN:L8N42P0X7 TEXT:"said"] in June it would cut 550 jobs as part of plans under [USN:SPN40B000 TEXT:"Brittin"] to save £500 million ($661 million) over the next three years. Channel 4, which cut its pre-tax deficit to £10 million in 2025, said last month it would cut about 340 jobs, representing more than a quarter of its workforce, in one of the biggest rounds of redundancies in its 43-year history. ($1 = 0.7569 pounds)

item.title: A 194-year-old tortoise, world's oldest land animal, may hold clues to longer life
item.description: The world's oldest-known terrestrial animal, an Aldabra giant tortoise named Jonathan and estimated to be about 194 years old, may owe his extraordinary longevity to a combination of genetic traits and an ability to keep key cellular systems functioning in a more youthful way, according to scientists.
item.dc:creator: Marta Serafinko
item.content:encoded: The world's oldest-known terrestrial animal, an Aldabra giant tortoise named Jonathan and estimated to be about 194 years old, may owe his extraordinary longevity to a combination of genetic traits and an ability to keep key cellular systems functioning in a more youthful way, according to scientists. Members of this species are known to live more than 100 years, but Jonathan has far exceeded that. Brought to the remote South Atlantic island of St Helena as a fully grown animal in 1882, likely from the Aldabra Atoll or the Granitic Seychelles, the tortoise now resides in a paddock at Plantation House, the governor's residence. "Other Aldabra tortoises have been claimed to have lived as long as Jonathan, but he has the most documentary evidence supporting his age," said Benjamin Vaisvil, a researcher affiliated with the organization Kallel and co-lead author of the study published on Wednesday in the journal Science Advances . Scientists have studied Jonathan to explore the secrets of the animal's amazing longevity, sequencing his genome and analysing his epigenome — the chemical markers that control which genes switch on and off. "We found changes in Jonathan's genome in pathways associated with longevity, like DNA repair, mitochondrial function, insulin regulation and telomere function," Vaisvil said. Mitochondria are structures considered the powerhouse of a cell. Insulin is a hormone that helps regulate levels of blood sugar by letting it enter the body's cells for energy. Telomeres are protective caps at the ends of chromosomes, structures that carry genetic information inside cell nuclei. Researchers compared Jonathan's epigenome with four other Aldabra tortoises, ranging from juveniles to older adults. While pretending to feed Jonathan, they waited until he began biting the air, then wedged his mouth open with a gloved hand and scraped under his tongue with a specialized kit. St Helena officials restrict blood draws to prevent infection risks. To explain the finding, Vaisvil compared the genome to a cookbook and the epigenome to handwritten notes in the margins. "As the cookbook ages, those notes become more difficult to read clearly. We can think of that as methylation entropy," Vaisvil said, referring to a metric for disorder in a certain biochemical process. Most of the notes in Jonathan's "cookbook" look very old. But in certain regions, stretches of DNA that act as switches controlling whether genes are turned on or off, Jonathan's methylation entropy was lower than that of every tortoise studied except a 5-year-old juvenile. These regions controlled genes that influence longevity. The researchers identified 287 genes with variants unique to Jonathan, including some linked to tumour suppression and DNA repair. The tortoise also carries extra copies of a gene that encodes a protein that hunts down ageing and cancerous cells. 'GENTLE GIANT' When younger, Jonathan was known for mischievous antics including overturning chairs and lying on croquet balls, according to the tortoise's longtime veterinarian and study co-author Joe Hollins. Cataracts have since left him mostly blind. Hollins describes Jonathan today as "a gentle giant." Determining how long giant tortoises can live is challenging because reliable historical records are scarce and many outlive researchers. Record-keeping before the 20th century also was problematic. While a young tortoise's age can be estimated from growth rings on the plates that form the animal's shell, ascertaining the age of adults is more difficult. The new study involved only one exceptionally old tortoise, making it hard to determine whether the traits identified are unique to Jonathan or common among long-lived tortoises. "We cannot say for certain that what we found is the reason for his longevity," Vaisvil said. Environmental factors also may have contributed. Jonathan lives on a tropical island, with an optimal diet carefully managed by trained veterinarians. The research findings broadly match patterns documented in studies of exceptionally long-lived people, suggesting that some mechanisms of aging may be shared across species. Vaisvil noted that a recent study of a 117-year-old woman found unusually efficient mitochondrial function, echoing findings in some of Jonathan's regions. VORACIOUS APPETITE Despite his age, Jonathan retains a voracious appetite, Hollins said, lifting his head and stretching out his long neck when the veterinarian calls out his name. "I know he knows me, knows my voice and my handling, and I also know it isn't love on his part but a recognition of the arrival of a feast," Hollins said. "And yet I, of course, don't mind. I have a huge affection for him." "He is a remarkable symbol. Icon, I know, is an overused word, but Guinness World Records has just given him 'icon' status this year," Hollins said. Beloved by island residents, Jonathan has lived through world wars and the rise and fall of empires. "He is symbolic of resilience, longevity, endurance, a persistent presence throughout huge historic events," Hollins said.

Belgian students rally over education costs in protests echoing France

Local media reported that 107 people were arrested in Belgium in recent days.

High school students hold placards and shout slogans as they take part in a spontaneous street protest against education reforms introduced by the Wallonia-Brussels Federation government and an increase in student fees, in Liege, Belgium, Oct 7, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Stephanie Lecocq)

FAST

LIEGE: Hundreds of students , inspired in part by education al unrest in neighbouring France , have taken to the streets of the Belgian city of Liège, with local media reporting 107 arrests in recent days. Local authorities could not immediately be reached to confirm the arrests, which the Belga news agency reported were linked to offences including property damage and arson. Students have protested over Belgium's French-language education system, citing rising education costs , over crowded classrooms and difficulties accessing study materials. They held signs with slogans including "It's a mess, we are fighting for a right! Not a privilege!" and "I chose education , not the hunger games!!".

The unrest follows June clashes between protesters and police in Brussels over education reforms, including a tuition increase for most students in Belgium's French-speaking Community to €1,194 (US$1,280) from €835. Videos circulating on social media in recent days showed shattered glass, fires and hundreds of mostly young protesters in Liège, while other footage showed police blocking roads. During Wednesday's (Oct 7) protest, police were seen checking students for weapons.

A person throws an object into a burning structure on a street, on the day of a spontaneous street protest of high school students against education reforms introduced by the Wallonia-Brussels Federation government and an increase in student fees, in Liege, Belgium, Oct 7, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Stephanie Lecocq)

IN TOUCH WITH FRENCH STUDENTS Some students told Reuters they were in touch with French counterparts. "We support each other because we're facing pretty much the same issues," 19-year-old student Alfred said. Amelia Di Salve, also 19, who is studying to become a teacher, said Belgium's student movement began earlier this year and was reignited after students saw the demonstrations in France . "When we saw nothing was changing without protests , we decided we would start ... France did influence us a little," she said. Liège mayor Willy Demeyer told Belgian broadcaster RTBF he hoped calm would return and "that dialogue can be established and that the young people can express their grievances in a peaceful way and, if possible, have those concerns heard".

item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: Wall Street ouvre en baisse, pénalisée par le pétrole et l'obligataire
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ouvre en baisse, pénalisée par le pétrole et l'obligataire 8 octobre (Reuters) - La Bourse de New York a ouvert en baisse jeudi, la progression des prix du pétrole maintenant la pression sur le marché obligataire, où les rendements avoisinant leurs plus hauts niveaux depuis plus de deux décennies. La BCE pourrait devoir procéder à de nouvelles hausses de taux, estime Dolenc LJUBLJANA, 8 octobre (Reuters) - La Banque centrale européenne (BCE) pourrait être contrainte de continuer à relever ses taux directeurs face au risque d'une aggravation de l'inflation mais le moment et l'ampleur d'une telle mesure restent bien trop incertains pour pouvoir être prédits, a déclaré Primož Dolenc, membre du Conseil des gouverneurs de l'institution de Francfort et gouverneur de la banque centrale slovène. Le gouvernement allemand relève ses prévisions de croissance pour 2026 et 2027 BERLIN, 8 octobre (Reuters) - Le gouvernement allemand a revu à la hausse ses prévisions économiques pour cette année et l'année prochaine, la guerre en Iran n'ayant pas un impact aussi sévère qu'initialement redouté, a déclaré jeudi le ministère de l'Economie. Zone euro: Les rendements obligataires se tendent encore LONDRES, 8 octobre (Reuters) - Les rendements obligataires de la zone euro enregistrent jeudi de nouvelles fortes tensions, dans un contexte de hausse des prix de l'énergie, les investisseurs continuant à se débarrasser des obligations des pays les plus endettés comme la France et l'Italie, provoquant un creusement des "spreads" dans le bloc. Aux yeux du patron de Ryanair, le coût du kérosène restera élevé une année de plus BRUXELLES/LONDRES, 8 octobre (Reuters) - Les compagnies aériennes européennes vont connaître une nouvelle année de coûts de carburant élevés et de taris en hausse, la guerre en Iran maintenant les prix du kérosène à un niveau supérieur d'environ 50% à celui d'avant le conflit, a déclaré jeudi Michael O'Leary, directeur général de Ryanair. Le choc géopolitique se répercute désormais sur les marchés financiers, selon Moulin (BCE) FRANCFORT, 8 octobre (Reuters) - La quasi-totalité du choc inflationniste subi par l'Europe cette année est liée à l'énergie, mais les chocs géopolitiques à l'origine de la flambée des prix "se traduisent désormais par un choc financier", a déclaré jeudi Emmanuel Moulin, gouverneur de la Banque de France (BdF) et membre de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE). BCE-Wunsch contre un relèvement du ratio de réserves obligatoires des banques FRANCFORT, 8 octobre (Reuters) - La projet de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) visant à relever le ratio de réserves obligatoires imposé aux banques commerciales pourrait nuire à la crédibilité de ses futures opérations, voire empiéter sur la politique budgétaire des Etats, a déclaré jeudi Pierre Wunsch, membre du Conseil des gouverneurs de l'institution de Francfort et gouverneur de la Banque nationale de Belgique. Allemagne: Baisse surprise des exportations en août 8 octobre (Reuters) - Les exportations allemandes ont baissé de façon inattendue en août, accusant un recul de 0,8% par rapport au mois précédent, selon les données de l'Office fédéral de la statistique publiées jeudi. PepsiCo revoit à la baisse de ses prévisions, annonce de nouvelles réductions des coûts 8 octobre (Reuters) - PepsiCo a annoncé jeudi son intention de mettre en œuvre de nouvelles mesures de réduction des coûts après avoir revu à la baisse ses prévisions de bénéfice annuel récurrent, en raison d'une demande atone pour ses snacks et ses boissons en Amérique du Nord et de la hausse des coûts des matières premières. Tesco relève son objectif de bénéfice après une hausse au S1 LONDRES, 8 octobre (Reuters) - Tesco a revu à la hausse jeudi la fourchette basse de ses prévisions de bénéfice annuel, après avoir annoncé une hausse de 6,5% de son profit au premier semestre, malgré l'impact des épisodes caniculaires sur les volumes de vente dans l'ensemble du secteur.

item.title: OFRTP Summary
item.description: Nobel/Littérature: Le prix décerné à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nobel/Littérature: Le prix décerné à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson STOCKHOLM, 7 octobre (Reuters) - Le prix Nobel de littérature a été décerné jeudi à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson pour "son oeuvre audacieuse et inventive qui, dans un dialogue ludique avec la tradition classique, a créé de nouvelles formes pour la littérature contemporaine", a annoncé jeudi l'Académie royale des sciences de Suède. France-Dix millions de barils de gazole libérés des réserves pour baisser les prix à la pompe-Lecornu PARIS, 7 octobre (Reuters) - La France va libérer 10 millions de barils de gazole de ses réserves stratégiques avec l'objectif d'agir sur les prix à la pompe, qui devraient ainsi "mécaniquement baisser" de 12 centimes à 18 centimes d'euro par litre de gazole, a déclaré mercredi soir le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu. Le Danemark accuse la Russie d'actes de sabotage contre ses entreprises du secteur de la défense COPENHAGUE, 7 octobre (Reuters) - La Russie a lancé des opérations de sabotage contre des entreprises danoises fournissant l'Ukraine après avoir conclu que ses tentatives de perturbation à plus grande échelle n'avaient pas freiné le soutien militaire occidental à Kyiv, a déclaré mercredi une responsable des services de renseignement danois. Nuñez suspend l'usage des grenades assourdissantes contre les lycéens L'usage des grenades assourdissantes par les forces de l'ordre est suspendu "dans le cadre du mouvement lycéen", a annoncé mercredi sur RTL le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez. De plus en plus d'enfants non accompagnés empruntent des voies dangereuses pour rejoindre l'Europe, selon l'Onu Plus des deux tiers des enfants réfugiés et migrants qui ont rejoint l'Europe par les routes de la Méditerranée et des Balkans en 2025 étaient non accompagnés et bon nombre d'entre eux ont été victimes d'exploitation, selon un rapport publié mercredi par des agences des Nations Unies. La France ne peut plus se permettre la moindre erreur sur ses finances publiques dit Citadel La France ne peut plus se permettre la moindre erreur dans l'assainissement de ses finances publiques et la pression exercée par les marchés devrait inciter le gouvernement à se concentrer sur la maîtrise des dépenses à l'approche de l'élection présidentielle de 2027, a déclaré à Reuters Angel Ubide, économiste chez la société de gestion d'actifs Citadel. Nobel/Chimie-Le Français Henri Kagan et le Japonais Kenso Soai distingués pour avoir résolu le mystère des molécules "images miroir" Le prix Nobel de chimie a été décerné mercredi à Henri Kagan et à Kenso Soai pour avoir résolu une énigme de longue date sur la manière de former une seule des deux "images miroir" d'une molécule, une découverte d'une grande importance pour la fabrication de médicaments, a annoncé mercredi l'Académie royale des sciences de Suède. États-Unis: Christa Pike est consciente et capable de parler selon ses avocats Christa Pike, dont l'exécution a échoué la semaine dernière dans le Tennessee, a repris conscience et retrouvé l'usage de la parole, ont déclaré ses avocats dans un communiqué publié mardi soir. Marine Le Pen veut ramener le déficit budgétaire à 3% d'ici 2030 La candidate du Rassemblement national pour l'élection présidentielle 2027 en France, Marine Le Pen, a déclaré mardi qu'elle souhaitait ramener le déficit budgétaire du pays à 3% d'ici 2030, invitant le pays à faire les "bons choix" sous peine de perdre son autonomie financière. La Russie assure à l'OMS qu'il n'y a aucun cas de peste en Sibérie Les autorités russes ont assuré mardi à l'Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) qu'il n'y avait aucun cas de peste dans la ville d'Irkoutsk, en Sibérie, où une employée de laboratoire d'un institut de recherche sur la peste est décédée la semaine dernière.
